value.0: Primal Overrun. You already put it through the den and out the other side. Nothing left in these thickets tests you the way that did. Go run with your beast; that is the whole lesson now.

Stop. Right there. One more careless step and the ground under you remembers you different than it does now. You have not bonded deep enough with a beast to walk this den yet. Come back when the two of you move like one animal, not two.

So you did not flinch. Good, flinching gets you killed twice as fast in there. My clan lost the Grotto Apex Den three generations back to handlers who broke every beast they touched instead of binding it. Their newest, the adepts, drive young beasts on false charges just to watch something bleed. Go into the den on Dathomir, put down six of them, and bring me back the Primal Overrun Grotto Track Slate they keep. It still reads clan trails, even in their hands.
Take this. It opens the old slide-gate at the den's low mouth; the clan mark is still carved there if you look. Get in, get the slate, get out. Do not linger to admire anything.

The den was ours before the handlers came in from off-world with their goad-sticks and their contracts. They did not want the beasts tamed, just broken and pointed. We fought for it once and lost good hunters to beasts that had stopped being beasts. I do not go back in for pride. I go in when the den asks for a debt paid, and right now it is asking through you.

Every clan hunter that ever ran that den left a mark on a slate like that: where the good trails run, where the ground lies to you. The adepts use it to route beasts onto killing floors instead of hunting ground. Bring it back whole and it goes back to reading trails instead of routing slaughter.

Adepts, mostly. Loud, proud, and sloppy with beasts that do not trust them yet. That works against them as much as for you; a beast driven wrong turns on its own handler as easy as you. Watch the ground, not just the fight.
The den has not finished with you. Six adepts, and my slate off whichever one of them is still holding it when you are done.
You made it out and you are not missing pieces. That is already better than the last two off-worlders who tried. Let's see the slate.
That is clan work, done right. The trails still remember how to read true because of it. Rest up. There is more of this if you want it, and I think you do.

Slate came back clean. That is one debt closer to paid. The den's specialists are worse than adepts; they have stopped pretending their beasts choose anything. Put down five of them in the Grotto Apex Den and bring me the Primal Overrun Resonant Fang Charm off whichever one still has it hanging around its neck when it goes down.
Same gate, deeper trail this time. The slide-gate key still opens for you; the den does not forget a hand it has already let through. Go quiet, come back with the charm.

Adepts still flinch. Specialists trained the flinch out of themselves and their beasts both. They have turned Primal Overrun into something you do to an animal, not with one. A charge that is not chosen is not a charge, it is a shove. I want that shove stopped before it becomes a habit that outlives the den.

The resonant fang charm hums when a beast is about to break its bond and just run wild: old clan trick, to know the difference between fear and fury before it is too late to matter. The specialists wear it just to feel that hum and keep pushing anyway. Cruelty with a warning bell they ignore on purpose.

Because the last time I went into that den my own beast did not come out, and I put down what came out instead of him. I can send you. I cannot send myself back through that gate yet. Maybe not ever. That is mine to carry, not yours to fix.
Five specialists still walking around in there like they own the ground. Bring me that fang charm when they do not.
You have got their hum on you; I can feel it from here. Hand it over before it starts working on you too.
Good. The warning bell is back where it belongs. You are starting to move like someone the den might actually let leave twice.

You have done more in that den than most clan-born manage. There is a warden past the specialists, the one who trained them all to shove instead of bond. It has killed alone before, and it will kill you alone too. Do not go at it solo; bring two you would trust to carry your beast out if you cannot. Put it down and bring me the Primal Overrun Cracked Apex Totem it carries.
Gate is the same. Ground past it is not; the warden does not wait for you to be ready, so do not wait either. Go in together, come out together.

One of ours, once. Best hand with a beast I ever trained besides myself. The handlers did not break him; they paid him, and he decided the shove worked better than the bond. He is the reason the specialists shove instead of ask. Cut that off at the root.

The cracked apex totem used to mark a den's true alpha trail, back when the den had one worth marking. He carries it broken because he broke it himself, on purpose, the day he stopped being clan. Bring it back whole enough to read and I will know the trail again.

Because he does not tire and he does not miss, and a beast that has been shoved instead of bonded does not know how to quit either. One hunter goes down alone against that and the den gets a new pair of bones to remember. Two more blades beside yours, and he has to split his attention between three throats instead of one. That is not cowardice. That is how the den has always hunted anything worth calling an alpha.
The warden is still down there teaching the wrong lesson. Go finish it, with company, like I said.
You are standing. All three of you, I hope, wherever the rest of your hunt is now. Let's see what he was carrying.
The apex totem, whole and readable. That is the first true blow against what this den became. Rest. The inner circle will have felt this.

Four are left who matter: the inner circle, the ones who taught the warden his shove and taught it to everyone under him since. They hold the deep floor together, not alone, so do not you go alone either. Put all four down and bring me the Primal Overrun Den-Mother's Fang Token they keep between them.
Same gate. They will have heard about the warden by now, so expect them ready for you. Go in together, stay together; that is not a suggestion with four of them.

They run the den now that the warden has gone quiet. Four voices deciding which beasts get shoved next, which trails get burned into killing floors. They learned cruelty as doctrine, and they teach it like doctrine: patient, repeatable, wrong.

Every den worth the name has a den-mother somewhere back in its bones, the first beast the clan ever bonded true, not broken. Her fang token was passed hunter to hunter as proof you knew the difference. The inner circle split it four ways so no one hunter could ever claim it again. Whole in your hand, it is proof the difference still means something.

Nothing like what they teach. A proper overrun is your beast choosing the same target you already chose, same breath, same moment, not a beast driven at something because a stick told it to. You will know it when it happens with yours. It feels like agreement, not a shove.
Four voices still running that den like it is theirs to run. Go quiet them, together, and bring the token back whole.
Company is still breathing, and so are you. That token had better be in one piece. Hand it here.
Whole, and warm, like it has been waiting. One voice left down there, and it is the one that made all the others. The trail is short now, so I will say it plain: you have earned this last one.

Last one. The master is the reason the den forgot what an overrun is supposed to feel like; every shove the others taught, he wrote first. He fights the same way you are about to fight, if you finish this: beast and hunter moving as one push. Bring your two back, because his overrun does not slow down for numbers, and one hunter alone just becomes one more body the den has to explain. The den keeps no token for this. His fall is the proof, all of it.
Then go. Gate is open same as always. This is the one I cannot tell you how to win, only that you will not, alone.

The others copied pieces of the overrun. He never lost the whole of it; he just aimed it at cruelty instead of company. What you have been chasing this whole trial, the true version, the one your own beast is starting to feel with you, he still has. That is what makes him dangerous. That is also what you are about to take from him.

Because an overrun is a beast and a hunter agreeing to move at once, and his beast agrees with him faster than any one of you can answer alone. Three throats coming at him from three angles, he has to choose, and choosing is the one thing that technique was never built to do twice in a breath. Alone, you are just the next thing he does not have to choose between.

It goes back to being a den instead of a lesson in cruelty. Whether my clan ever walks back in, I do not know yet. That part is mine to decide, after. Yours is just to make sure there is a den left worth deciding about.
He is still down there, still teaching it wrong. Go end the lesson. Together.
Quiet. The whole den has gone quiet, and it has never once done that in my lifetime. Tell me it is him.

Then it is done, and it is yours: the overrun the way it is supposed to run, beast and hunter, one push, one choice. My clan lost this den three generations back. You just gave me a reason to think about walking through that gate again myself. Go run with your beast. You have earned the ground under both of you.
Back to it.
I'll clear the six and bring your slate.
What happened to your clan's den?
What's this track slate to you?
What am I walking into down there?
Not today. I need to think.
Here's the Primal Overrun Grotto Track Slate.
Back to it.
I'll take the five specialists.
What makes a specialist worse than an adept?
What's the fang charm for?
Why can't you go in yourself?
Give me time first.
Here's the Primal Overrun Resonant Fang Charm.
Back to it.
I'll bring company and take the warden down.
Who is this warden to you?
What's the apex totem?
Why do I need help for one target?
Not until I've got my two.
Here's the Primal Overrun Cracked Apex Totem, whole.
Back to it.
I'll take my company back in for the four.
What do the inner circle actually do?
What's the den-mother's fang token?
What does a proper overrun feel like?
My company needs rest first.
Here's the Primal Overrun Den-Mother's Fang Token, whole.
Back to it.
We're going in for the master.
What makes him different from the warden and the circle?
Why does his overrun need three of us and not one?
What happens to the den, after?
Not until my company's ready.
It's done. He's down.
